$comment: What the compatibility matrix (Strategy §145, plan step N4.5) says beyond the suite's areas: each capability's status on WitOS, the step or milestone that gives it, and the fact behind the status. compatibility-matrix renders this with the suite's checks and expectations.json into @Docs/Implementation/Compatibility-Matrix.md; a host test requires the document to be current. A status is Supported, Partial, Absent or Planned.

capabilities.name: CoreCLR with the JIT, `Reflection.Emit`, `AssemblyLoadContext`
capabilities.note: Every method is compiled into the double mapping of a shared memory file; upstream's PAL suite and slices of its runtime and library tests pass in the guest.

capabilities.name: Shared framework through `dotnet App.dll`
capabilities.note: The install under `/dotnet` as the shared-framework packaging lays it out; an application the stock SDK publishes without a RID runs unchanged.

capabilities.name: .NET 8 and .NET 10 side by side
capabilities.note: `release/8.0` with its own patch set beside `release/10.0`; `rollForward` and `--roll-forward` select the framework. On x64 and ARM64: `release/8.0` is not built for riscv64, whose upstream port came after it (V3).

capabilities.name: NativeAOT
capabilities.note: The system's own tool for the services of the boot package, not the application contract.

capabilities.name: Garbage collector
capabilities.note: The workstation and the server collector, the server one with a heap per processor (P2), each with its heap bounded to 75% of what a process may own (`DOTNET_GCTotalPhysicalMemory`).

capabilities.name: Globalization with ICU
capabilities.note: ICU4C 78.3 built from the pinned source; invariant mode only where an application asks for it.

capabilities.name: Time zones
capabilities.note: `TimeZoneInfo` from pinned tzdata under `/usr/share/zoneinfo`; `/etc/localtime` is UTC.

capabilities.name: Files and directories on volumes
capabilities.note: ext4 (written through the journal), FAT and `/tmp` through the namespace service; modes and times as the volume keeps them; the boot package read-only.

capabilities.name: Memory-mapped files
capabilities.note: A private mapping is a copy, a shared one shows the service's pages; `MemoryMappedFile` works, the copy's cost is the file's size.

capabilities.name: File change notifications (`FileSystemWatcher`)
capabilities.note: `PlatformNotSupportedException`: the namespace service sends none.

capabilities.name: Processes (`Process.Start`, `WaitForExit`, redirected streams, `Kill`)
capabilities.note: `posix_spawn` over the process manager with pipes between processes; no process enumeration, no other process's name or times, no signal but `SIGKILL`, one user, no process groups.

capabilities.name: Console and terminal
capabilities.note: The terminal service over the virtio console with Linux's line discipline: `ReadLine`, `ReadKey`, `KeyAvailable`, `CancelKeyPress`, the window size; without a terminal the standard streams are the kernel log.

capabilities.name: PowerShell 7 (upstream, `dotnet pwsh.dll`, PSReadLine)
capabilities.note: 7.6.7's framework-dependent archive runs unchanged from the data volume with libpsl-native built from the pinned source: the version table, pipelines, files on volumes, `Get-Date`, `Get-ChildItem` and an interactive session under PSReadLine on the terminal (RFC 0020 §57.2–57.5); process enumeration fails explicitly, as the Processes row says.

capabilities.name: C# in the console (CSharpRepl) and the .NET SDK
capabilities.note: CSharpRepl 0.9.2 runs unchanged from the data volume's layer over the .NET SDK 10.0.300 laid there as a base application, which `dotnet` finds through `/data/global.json` (the `runtime-csharprepl` scenario: expressions, classes, files of the volume, `#load`, a compiler's error); `dotnet build` in a session is measured, not gated, and `#r "nuget:"` waits for a feed on the volume or the network (W). The SDK's publication is per RID (its ReadyToRun code over the IL), so the layer takes the linux-x64 archive on x64 and the linux-arm64 one on ARM64; the scenario passes on x64, waits on ARM64 for S8.2 (CoreCLR relocates the arm64 images' code through a writable and executable window WitOS never grants), and riscv64, for which no SDK is published, has none.

capabilities.name: Text console on a display (framebuffer, keyboard)
capabilities.note: The firmware's framebuffer (ramfb, 800 by 600 on both boards) is a device of the firmware bus (C2.1), the display service draws the terminal on it with a pinned bitmap font (Spleen 8 by 16, 100 by 37 cells) and takes the virtio keyboard's keys (C2.2), the terminal mirrors its one session on the display and the serial console, which stays the recovery console, and upstream PowerShell runs on that screen with the keyboard on both ISAs (C2.3, the `runtime-display` scenario); the layout is US until the input model of M9, and colours are drawn in a 16-colour palette (C2.6).

capabilities.name: Full-screen console applications (TUI)
capabilities.note: The display's emulator draws SGR's colours and attributes, the alternate screen and the cursor's visibility, swallows the string sequences and answers the device attributes and the size (C2.6); Arlecchino.Commander, built from its source as a base application, lists, views and copies files on the screen through the keyboard (C4.2, the `runtime-commander` scenario); Terminal.Gui's UICatalog 2.5.0 runs with `--disable-cm`, since its configuration watcher needs file change notifications, and CSharpFar needs `HttpClient` at its start, which waits for networking.

capabilities.name: Named synchronization objects (`Mutex` with a name)
capabilities.note: Under `/tmp/.dotnet` in the namespace service's `/tmp`.

capabilities.name: Cryptography
capabilities.note: OpenSSL 3.5, the long-term support series, built by the system layer from its pinned release for each ISA (no-asm, no engines of the kernel): the algorithms, X.509 and chains through System.Security.Cryptography's unix flavour, as on Linux (the suite's Cryptography area); the root store is Mozilla's CA bundle at `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`, which the store reads as one file.

capabilities.name: Networking (`Socket`, `HttpClient`)
capabilities.note: IPv4 and IPv6 sockets over the network service's managed stack: TCP, UDP, the loopback, dual-stack `AF_INET6` sockets with IPv4 peers in the mapped form, a link-local and a global IPv6 address from the router's advertisement (W4.3), names through musl's resolver, `HttpClient` over HTTP/1.1 (W2.2) and `SslStream` and HTTPS over the OpenSSL the system layer builds (W3.1; the suite's Network area). Not served: multicast group membership, ancillary data, raw sockets, keep-alive probes. Unix domain sockets since W4.1 (the next row).

capabilities.name: Local sockets and named pipes (`UnixDomainSocketEndPoint`, `NamedPipeServerStream`)
capabilities.note: AF_UNIX stream and sequenced-packet sockets and socketpair, the libc's own: a path below a mount point or an abstract name, connections within a process and between processes, named pipes as on Unix (the suite's Ipc area). A socket's name lives in the namespace service, beside the volume's entries, and is gone at the next boot; no descriptors pass over a socket.

capabilities.name: ASP.NET Core
capabilities.note: The shared framework Microsoft.AspNetCore.App in the install, built IL alone from its pinned source for every ISA; an ordinary Kestrel application published without a RID serves HTTP and HTTPS over the network service's sockets and answers the runner through the port forward (`runtime-aspnetcore`). No ReadyToRun code: the framework starts under the JIT.

capabilities.name: Diagnostics (`createdump`, EventPipe, `dotnet-dump`)
capabilities.note: The runtime's diagnostic IPC over a Unix domain socket: a tool reaches a process through the port it starts with (`DOTNET_DiagnosticPorts`; the Ipc area's DiagnosticsIpc). Every process's id is 1, so the default port has one name and the first .NET process takes it. No `createdump`; the debugger story decides the rest.

capabilities.name: Compression (`System.IO.Compression`)
capabilities.note: zlib-ng and brotli in-tree.

capabilities.name: Server GC and several scheduling processors
capabilities.note: Threads run on every processor of the board with their affinity honoured (P1); `Environment.ProcessorCount`, `Thread.GetCurrentProcessorId`, the server collector's heaps and the thread pool see every processor, and the scenarios of N1 and N2 run on four (P2).

capabilities.name: Network interfaces and their changes (System.Net.NetworkInformation)
capabilities.note: `NetworkInterface.GetAllNetworkInterfaces`, an interface's addresses, hardware address, index, MTU and DNS servers, `GetIsNetworkAvailable` and `NetworkChange`'s subscriptions work as on Linux: the libc answers the netlink route socket and the `SIOCGIF*` ioctls from the network service's configuration (the loopback and `eth0` with the lease), and a change of the lease reaches the sockets that listen. The gateways are empty and the statistics fail, since Linux's files read them from `/proc/net`, which is not emulated; a link's loss is not reported (Compatibility-Differences: Network interfaces).

capabilities.name: Avalonia and other GUI frameworks
capabilities.note: Needs the presentation layer of RFC 0009.

hardware.note: Every gate runs on it; a step closes only when the three ISAs pass.

Since V3: the kernel (V1), layer 2 (V2.1–V2.3) and the Unix-form runtime (V2.4) pass there, every scenario of runtime-witos among them, and the applications published on Windows run unchanged with every check of the suite as recorded (runtime-published); a step closes only when the three ISAs pass. The NuGet libraries' own suites (N2.2) and .NET 8 beside .NET 10 (N3) stay on x64 and ARM64.
After phase V; firmware memory reclamation and the hardware matrix of Strategy §146.
